Follow this guide to get your local development environment up and running. 📋 Prerequisites Before cloning and running the application, ensure you have the following software installed: .NET 10.0 SDK (or higher) An IDE or Code Editor: Visual Studio 2026 (Windows-only) JetBrains Rider (Cross-platform) VS Code with the C# Dev Kit extension (Cross-platform) A modern web browser (Edge, Chrome, Firefox) 🛠️ Local Setup Instructions 1. Clone the Repository Open your terminal and run the following command to clone the project: git clone https://github.com/DrittesPhantom/BlazorWebAppTemplate cd BlazorWebAppTemplate 2. Install Workloads Install the wasm-tools workload by running: dotnet workload install wasm-tools --skip-manifest-update --configfile src/NuGet.Config 3. Restore Dependencies Restore the NuGet packages using the .NET CLI: dotnet restore 4. Run the Application Navigate to the main project directory and start the development server: dotnet run --project src/Template.UI/Template.UI.csproj Once started, open your browser and navigate to https://localhost:5098 or Ctrl+Click on the link shown in the terminal. 📝 Building the Documentation Locally If you want to preview changes made to these markdown files locally, ensure you have the DocFX CLI installed, if not run: dotnet tool install -g docfx Then run: docfx docs/docfx.json --serve Once started, open your browser and navigate to http://localhost:8080 or Ctrl+Click on the link shown in the terminal. ↩ Back to Main Website
